findings.title: Calendar/video deletion promises are detached during rescheduling
findings.body: Using `forEach(async ...)` discards every callback promise. Because `getCalendar` now always awaits a dynamic-import promise before `deleteEvent` is invoked, this function proceeds to send the reschedule email and returns without waiting for deletion to start or finish. Rejections from either the import or the provider deletion also bypass the surrounding `try/catch` and can become unhandled rejections. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` (or an awaited `for...of`) so cancellation is completed and failures are handled before the operation finishes.

findings.title: Calendar/video deletion promises are detached during rescheduling
findings.body: Using `forEach(async ...)` discards every callback promise. Since `getCalendar` now yields at the dynamic import, the reschedule flow can return and send its email before calendar deletion has even been invoked; import/provider failures are not caught by the surrounding `try/catch` and may be unhandled. Await a mapped `Promise.all` or use an awaited loop to ensure these integration cancellations run deterministically and errors are handled.

findings.title: Reschedule mutation does not await dynamic calendar deletion
findings.body: The async callback passed to `forEach` is not awaited. With the new `await getCalendar(...)`, every calendar deletion is deferred past the callback's first await, while the mutation immediately sends the reschedule email and can complete successfully. A failed dynamic import or `deleteEvent` call is also detached from the mutation and has no error handler. Replace this with an awaited `Promise.all` over the filtered references (and handle its errors as appropriate).
